intended_object: Positive (degree-one) homogeneity of an extended-nonnegative operator T on L0Infinity: for every real a > 0, every f and every x, T(a·f)(x) = a·T(f)(x), including when the value is ∞. This comes from the name, the docstring, the module doc ("exact positive-homogeneity normalization"), and the sibling definition `SchwartzNonnegativeOperator.PositivelyHomogeneous`.
explanation:
The body says `T (scaleL0Infinity a f) x = T f x` for all a > 0. The factor `ENNReal.ofReal a` is missing on the right-hand side. That makes it scale invariance (homogeneity of degree 0), not positive homogeneity.

Concrete discrepancy: take T f x = ENNReal.ofReal ‖f x‖, which is measurable and positively homogeneous. With a = 2 and f(0) = 1, T(2f)(0) = 2 but T f (0) = 1, so this T fails the definition. Conversely, a constant operator T f x = 1 satisfies the definition, but it is not positively homogeneous.

The sibling definition `SchwartzNonnegativeOperator.PositivelyHomogeneous` in SchwartzModularOperator.lean has the correct form `T (a • f) x = ENNReal.ofReal a * T f x`. The intended use also needs degree-one homogeneity. In `operatorLevelSet_scale_inv`, normalizing the level set at height α to height 1 relies on T(α⁻¹f) = α⁻¹·T f. With the definition as written, the level set at height 1 would be compared with the one at height α, which is false in general. Lacunary or Carleson maximal operators are degree-one homogeneous, not scale invariant. So the definition does not capture positive homogeneity.
